access_classes.means: Served the content to an anonymous browser.
Served a subscription or registration wall instead of the content. We hold no licence to go past it.
Served a bot or browser challenge (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, Vercel). The challenge page's hash is kept as the record.
Wants a signed-in account (some social posts).
Refused because of where the request came from.
404 or 410: the page no longer exists at this address.
5xx, a timeout, a DNS failure or a refused connection: the site is not answering. For the affected sites this is the finding.
Listed, but the watcher is told not to fetch it (licence or editorial decision).

tips.says: Their browser extension, php2shell-checker, was just approved on the Chrome Web Store. It checks whether a website runs outdated PHP or a supported PHP application such as WordPress. They describe it as privacy friendly and read-only, with nothing leaving the browser, and aimed at CISOs in the SME segment as easier than running scripts.
